hypothesis: A closed syntax profile can resolve an integer-return contract through explicit local import/call chains and invalidate its evidence key when only a helper changes, while refusing dynamic or incomplete ownership.
scope: Optional research observer, not the ordinary Ruby route, a general Python resolver, a package loader or neural training.

profile.modules: Operator-frozen flat module registry, module.py only; no packages, implicit import search or external resolution.
profile.module_statements: Optional leading docstring, explicit absolute from-imports of registered callable names, and simple function declarations; no other top-level statements.
profile.functions: Unique zero-argument synchronous functions with an optional leading docstring and one return. No decorators, annotations, defaults, assignments, globals, attributes, expressions with effects or conditional bodies.
profile.returns: An exact bounded integer literal or one zero-argument direct call to a uniquely bound local/imported function.
profile.ownership: All module names unique across imports and function declarations; every import target module and symbol must exist in the same admitted registry.
profile.dependency_key: Conservatively bind all registered source hashes, entry selector, profile version and extractor/workspace identity. Do not reuse a root-only source key.
profile.meaning: A conditional static result under the supplied closed profile, not proof of sys.modules, import hooks, monkeypatching or actual runtime binding.

development_cases: Duplicate binding in either declaration order
Attribute call, parameter passing or dynamic expression
Oversized source, depth and AST budget
measurements: Complete call edges and exact function quotations
Stable contract key for formatting-only changes
acceptance: No execution of inspected source; no positive result for unsupported, missing or ambiguous dependencies; current evidence binds the full supplied registry. No REMOVE decision is made by this observer.
evaluation_split: Development controls. Future actual-source applicability is reported separately; these cases are not an independent holdout.
